question: Should this release intentionally invalidate all affected cost-usage cache artifacts and pay a one-time rescan cost to correct offsets persisted under the previous EOF behavior?
rationale: Invalidation prevents stale offsets from suppressing completed records, but accepting the upgrade-time rescan cost is a release tradeoff requiring maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept rebuild after proof
options.body: Keep the version bumps and merge after redacted live output demonstrates tail recovery and cache reconstruction on a representative history.

options.title: Narrow invalidation
options.body: Reduce the bumped cache set only if maintainers can establish that particular providers or Pi artifacts never persisted offsets affected by this scanner behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept rebuild after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the version bumps and merge after redacted live output demonstrates tail recovery and cache reconstruction on a representative history.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history owns the scanner's incremental parsing and persisted cache-reuse behavior most directly.
